description: A longer (5-entry) hash-chained audit log must also detect tampering when the tampered entry is the LAST one in the chain, not just an early one -- proves detection is not coincidentally specific to index 1.

A full-chain-recompute tamper (mutate entry 1, then recompute every hash/prev_hash from index 0 forward so the chain stays internally self-consistent) is NOT detected by the plain hash chain alone, but IS detected when a checkpoint recorded before the tamper (at the last entry, index 2) is cross-checked -- this is the Phase 5 mechanism that closes the gap documented in docs/phase3_independent_audit.md Finding 4 and docs/phase5_audit_integrity.md.
